subject: Proposal: Availability Floor + Escalating Credit Bands
messages:
From: Elena Martinez <procurement@pulseworks.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement-team@pulseworks.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: baseline availability floor and monthly credit proposal

Hi Michael,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team at PulseWorks is excited about Redwood's throughput improvements for our batched summarization jobs. Before we move to legal, Procurement needs the SLA baseline clarified for our executive signoff.

Specifically:
- We need an explicit minimum monthly availability floor (for the EU and US regions we use), not the higher enterprise uptime you posted in the public doc. For our use pattern (heavy batch inference overnight), we can't reliably meet a 99.95% expectation. Can Redwood commit to a 99.6% monthly availability floor for the first 6 months?
- If availability drops below that floor, we want a simple monthly credit schedule (percent of monthly invoice) so our finance team can model risk. PulseWorks proposes: 5% credit if monthly availability is 99.0–99.59%, 15% if 98.0–98.99%, 30% if <98.0%.
- We will accept standard maintenance carveouts, but want a cap on scheduled maintenance per month (no more than 6 hours without prior written agreement).

I've attached our procurement note (PulseWorks_SLA_ask.pdf) with the ask in a numbered list. Can you confirm whether Redwood is willing to accept a temporary (6-month) availability floor of 99.6 with a credit schedule broadly similar to the one above? If not, please propose alternatives — we prefer a simple, predictable monthly credit formula rather than a complex pro-rata system.

Best,
Elena Martinez
Director of Procurement
PulseWorks

Hi Elena — really appreciate the clear ask and the context on batch windows. Short answer: we can be flexible, but we need to align on measurement method, carveouts, and a cap on credits so it's operationally sustainable for both sides.

Proposal from Redwood (high level):
- Standard public SLA: 99.9% monthly availability. For your batched workload profile we can offer a temporary floor of 99.6% for the first 3 months of production (pilot). After the pilot we'll review; if patterns are stable we can extend to 6 months.
- Credit bands (monthly invoice %):
  - >= 99.9%: 0% credit
  - 99.6%–99.89%: 8% credit
  - 99.0%–99.59%: 20% credit
  - < 99.0%: 40% credit (subject to maximum monthly cap)
- Monthly credit cap: credits will not exceed 100% of that month's hosting charges (hard cap).
- Measurement: time-weighted region availability measured using Redwood's public telemetry, with a 10-minute granularity.
- Maintenance carveouts: scheduled maintenance (>=48 hours notice) excluded. Emergency maintenance will be excluded if we publish a post-incident summary in 72 hours. We will not exceed 6 hours/month of planned maintenance without written agreement.

I've attached our redline (redwood_sla_redline_v2.pdf) with the legal-friendly wording and suggested replacement paragraph for the "Availability" section. Legal & CS copied on this thread to pull in exact definitions and operational commitments.

Next steps:
1) Laura to review and comment on definitions/wording.
2) Monica to confirm instrumentation, runbooks, and whether a 3-month pilot with weekly check-ins works for PulseWorks.
3) If you accept the pilot terms, we'll hand off to Legal to formalize.

Would you be available for a 30‑minute call tomorrow to align on measurement and carveouts?

Thanks — Michael

Elena / Michael — quick legal read. Thanks for laying this out. A few points we need to lock before we can sign off: 

1) Definitions: "Availability" must be defined as the percentage of successful inference requests over total attempted requests in the billing region, excluding requests that meet documented exclusion criteria (client-side errors 4xx, misrouted traffic, and scheduled maintenance windows). We'll propose the following language in the attached doc.

2) Measurement window: Monthly period = UTC first day 00:00 to last day 23:59:59. Credits calculated at month close. Disputes allowed within 30 days of invoice.

3) Scheduled maintenance: we can agree on a 6-hour monthly allowance only if Redwood publishes scheduled maintenance at least 48 hours in advance via the console and status.redwood.ai. If Redwood exceeds 6 hours without prior written agreement, downtime beyond 6 hours will count toward availability.

4) Emergency exceptions: emergency maintenance is excluded only if accompanied by an incident report within 72 hours that includes root cause and corrective action plan.

5) Cap / Aggregation: We prefer a per-account cap (100% of that month's recurring charges). If PulseWorks wants credits applicable to other bill types (consulting, one-offs), specify explicitly in the SOW.

I've attached legal comments (redwood_sla_legal_comments.docx) with proposed clause text. Michael: I tightened the band percentages to align with Redwood precedent (small change in band labels and the 40% top band).

If PulseWorks wants a simpler schedule (your suggested 5/15/30), we can discuss, but Redwood can't accept a structure that yields unlimited exposure without a monthly cap.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference
